title: Tax up to 100% of benefits for high earners
description: Beginning in 2031, for single/head-of-household/married-filing-separate taxpayers with MAGI of $250,000 or more and joint filers with MAGI of $500,000 or more, include up to the remaining 15 percent of Social Security benefits in taxable income (increased from up to 85 percent of benefits taxable under current law).
impacts: Increases taxation on high-income beneficiaries; Wage-indexed thresholds; Long-range effect: 0.22% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.19% of payroll

title: Eliminate taxation of benefits with phased thresholds
description: Eliminate federal income taxation of OASDI benefits that is credited to the OASI and DI Trust Funds for 2054 and later. Phase out OASDI taxation of benefits by increasing relevant income thresholds from 2045 through 2053, while maintaining Hospital Insurance Trust Fund revenue.
impacts: Reduces taxation of Social Security benefits; Phases out over 9 years; Long-range effect: -0.10% of payroll; 75th year effect: -0.01% of payroll

title: Simplify benefit taxation with fixed thresholds
description: Replace the current-law thresholds for federal income taxation of OASDI benefits with a single set of thresholds at $50,000 for single filers and $100,000 for joint filers for taxation of up to 85 percent of OASDI benefits, effective for tax year 2026. Thresholds would be fixed and not indexed.
impacts: Simplifies benefit taxation structure; Fixed income thresholds; Long-range effect: 0.02% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.02% of payroll

title: Reduce taxation of benefits by half
description: Reduce the portion of Social Security benefits subject to taxation from 85% to 42.5% for high earners and from 50% to 25% for moderate earners, phased in from 2025-2030. Continue to index current-law income thresholds by inflation.
impacts: Significantly reduces taxation on Social Security benefits; Long-range effect: -0.62% of payroll; 75th year effect: -1.11% of payroll

title: Index current thresholds to inflation
description: Index the income thresholds for taxation of OASDI benefits to inflation starting in 2027. Current-law thresholds are $25,000 for single filers and $32,000 for joint filers for up to 50% of benefits taxed and $34,000 for single filers and $44,000 for joint filers for up to 85% of benefits taxed.
impacts: Prevents tax bracket creep through inflation adjustment; Long-range effect: -0.16% of payroll; 75th year effect: -0.01% of payroll

title: Tax up to 100% of Social Security benefits above certain income thresholds
description: Tax up to 100% of Social Security benefits above certain income thresholds starting in 2025.
impacts: Increases revenue from higher-income beneficiaries; Progressive approach to funding; Long-range effect: 0.52% of payroll; 75th year effect: 0.59% of payroll; Long-range shortfall eliminated: 15%; 75th year shortfall eliminated: 13%
